name: Cognigy (acquired by NICE — now NiCE Cognigy)
tagline: A Düsseldorf-built, voice-first enterprise conversational AI platform acquired by NICE for ~$955M in 2025 — genuinely excellent reviews, best-in-class API extensibility, and real payment-processing capability, built for large contact centers rather than SMB storefronts.
tldr: Cognigy was founded in 2016 in Düsseldorf, Germany by Philipp Heltewig, Sascha Poggemann, and Benjamin Mayr, raised approximately $165M across five rounds (including a $100M Series C in June 2024), and was acquired by contact-center giant NICE Ltd. for approximately $955M in a deal announced July 2025 — it now operates as 'NiCE Cognigy,' a healthy, well-funded strategic acquisition rather than a distressed sale.

The platform has genuine voice/IVR-first roots, with dedicated telephony extensions for Amazon Connect, Avaya, AudioCodes, Twilio, Vonage, Sipgate, and 8x8, alongside website chat, WhatsApp, and other social channels via Sunshine Conversations.

A direct code search of Cognigy's official, open-source extensions repository confirms comprehensive CRM/helpdesk integrations — Salesforce, Salesforce Service Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Freshsales, HubSpot, ServiceNow, and SAP C4C — but confirms no native Shopify, WooCommerce, WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, or Webflow connector exists.

A genuinely substantive Stripe extension gives Cognigy-built agents real payment capability: looking up invoices and payment methods, creating payment intents, and processing refunds directly — a level of financial-transaction depth uncommon in this category.

Multi-language support is a real, well-documented differentiator: custom NLU models for 20+ languages plus a 'Universal Locale' feature using cross-lingual transfer to map intents across 100+ languages from training data in a single language.

Independent reviews are genuinely excellent (Capterra: 4.8/5 across 23 reviews; G2: approximately 4.6/5) with no serious complaint patterns found — criticism centers on ordinary enterprise-SaaS friction like a steep learning curve, documentation gaps, and pricing opacity rather than fraud, lockouts, or hostile support.
keyFeatures: Deep, historically-rooted voice/IVR capability with dedicated telephony extensions for Amazon Connect, Avaya, AudioCodes, Twilio, Vonage, Sipgate, and 8x8
'Flows' — a visual, node-based drag-and-drop workflow builder consistently praised in independent reviews as intuitive despite the platform's underlying depth
'Knowledge AI' — built-in Retrieval-Augmented Generation over uploaded documents and FAQs, with support for connecting third-party RAG systems
A published, documented hallucination-mitigation approach using relevance/distance scoring, source citations, and transparency metadata
A dedicated 'Handover to Human Agent' node that preserves conversation context, intent, and authentication status on transfer

'Cognigy Insights' — real-time customizable dashboards, a 'Step Explorer' for conversation drop-off analysis, a business-metrics 'Goals Dashboard,' and an OData interface for external BI tools
A genuinely open, developer-first extensibility layer: a documented REST API, a webhook endpoint node, an official JavaScript/TypeScript REST client, and a full Extensions SDK for custom nodes

faq.question: Is Cognigy still an independent company?
faq.answer: No — NICE Ltd., a major contact-center and CX software company, acquired Cognigy for approximately $955M in a deal announced July 2025, and it now operates as 'NiCE Cognigy.' Unlike some other acquisitions covered in this category, this reads as a healthy, well-funded strategic acquisition by an established industry player rather than a distressed sale, and NiCE's own recent release notes suggest continued, active investment in the product (including deeper native NICE integration).

faq.question: Is Cognigy good for voice and IVR use cases specifically?
faq.answer: Yes — this is Cognigy's historical strength and a genuine differentiator. It has dedicated telephony extensions for Amazon Connect, Avaya, AudioCodes, Twilio, Vonage, Sipgate, and 8x8, and markets itself around 'the complete spectrum of voice use cases, from conversational IVR, self-service, and outbound calling to agent assist and real-time translation on voice.'

faq.question: Does Cognigy integrate with Shopify or other ecommerce platforms?
faq.answer: No — a direct code search of Cognigy's official, open-source extensions repository confirms no native Shopify, WooCommerce, WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, or Webflow connector exists. It does support BigCommerce and commercetools natively. A business could theoretically build a custom connector via Cognigy's generic REST/webhook nodes, but there's no prebuilt, out-of-the-box integration for the major SMB ecommerce/CMS platforms.

faq.question: Can Cognigy actually process payments or refunds?
faq.answer: Yes, genuinely — its official Stripe extension exposes real flow nodes for getting and creating customers, retrieving payment methods, getting and paying invoices, creating payment intents, retrieving products and charges, and creating refunds. This is a substantive, verified capability, uncommon in depth for this category.

faq.question: How much does Cognigy cost?
faq.answer: Cognigy has never published pricing — it's a fully enterprise, sales-quote-only model. Third-party estimates (which we could not verify against any primary source) suggest typical annual contracts starting around $300,000, with one estimate citing an average around $115,000 and a maximum around $350,000. At least one reviewer directly described the pricing model as 'too expensive for SMBs,' consistent with its enterprise-only positioning.

faq.question: What do independent reviews say about Cognigy?
faq.answer: Genuinely excellent — Capterra shows 4.8/5 across 23 verified reviews and G2 shows approximately 4.6/5. Reviewers repeatedly praise the intuitive Flows builder, powerful NLU, and strong support/training, while criticism centers on a steep learning curve for advanced JavaScript/API-level customization, documentation gaps, and a reporting dashboard some technical reviewers consider basic or outdated relative to competitors — ordinary enterprise-SaaS friction, not fraud, lockouts, or hostile support.

pricingBreakdown: Cognigy has never published pricing and operates on a fully enterprise, sales-quote-only model — consistent across every source we checked. Third-party estimates, which we could not verify against any Cognigy-published figure, suggest typical annual contracts commonly starting around $300,000, with one source citing figures ranging from an average around $115,000 to a maximum around $350,000. At least one independent reviewer directly stated the pricing model is 'too expensive for SMBs,' which is consistent with — and arguably an honest reflection of — Cognigy's deliberate enterprise-only positioning rather than a deceptive pricing practice. If your organization is smaller than a large enterprise contact center, budget accordingly or expect this platform to be out of reach; if you fit the enterprise profile, expect a substantial negotiated sales cycle rather than a self-serve rate card.

capabilities.note: This is Cognigy's most historically rooted and consistently validated strength — dedicated telephony extensions spanning Amazon Connect, Avaya, AudioCodes, Twilio, Vonage, Sipgate, and 8x8 give it real credibility for contact-center voice automation that many chat-first competitors in this category simply don't have.

Worth highlighting specifically: a direct inspection of Cognigy's official Stripe extension confirms real, substantive payment-processing nodes — invoice lookup, payment-intent creation, and refund processing — a level of genuine financial-transaction depth that's rare in this category and goes well beyond a typical 'order status lookup' integration.

Directly confirmed via code search rather than inference: no native Shopify, WooCommerce, WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, or Webflow connector exists in Cognigy's official extension catalog. This reflects Cognigy's enterprise-contact-center focus rather than a quality gap — a business on one of these platforms should look elsewhere for native support, not assume Cognigy will fit.

Worth contrasting explicitly with some other transitions covered in this category: NICE's ~$955M acquisition of Cognigy in 2025 reads as a well-funded strategic move by an established, major CX company, with recent release notes suggesting continued active investment (including deeper native NICE integration) rather than a wind-down or distressed sale.

Cognigy Insights is a real, documented analytics suite, but multiple independent, technically sophisticated reviewers specifically describe the reporting dashboard as basic or outdated relative to competitors — a genuine gap between the marketed feature set and day-to-day reporting experience worth flagging directly.

verdict: Cognigy is a genuinely strong platform for the enterprise contact center it's built for, and its acquisition by NICE for roughly $955M in 2025 — now operating as NiCE Cognigy — reads as a healthy, well-funded strategic move rather than the kind of distressed transition we've flagged for other tools in this category. Its voice/IVR roots are real and well-documented, with dedicated telephony extensions spanning the major CCaaS and PBX providers, and its Stripe integration gives it a genuinely uncommon level of payment-processing depth — invoice lookup, payment-intent creation, and refund processing — verified directly by inspecting the extension's code rather than taking marketing claims at face value. Multi-language support is a real differentiator too, with cross-lingual intent transfer covering 100+ languages from single-language training data. Independent reviews back all of this up convincingly: 4.8/5 on Capterra and roughly 4.6/5 on G2, with no serious complaint patterns anywhere we could verify. Where the rubric scores drop sharply, it's worth being direct that this reflects who Cognigy isn't built for, not a quality failure: a direct code search of its official extensions repository confirms no native Shopify, WooCommerce, WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, or Webflow integration exists, and pricing is fully enterprise, sales-quote-only, with at least one reviewer explicitly calling it too expensive for SMBs. If you're a large enterprise contact center — especially one with real voice/IVR volume and an existing Salesforce, Zendesk, Dynamics, or ServiceNow deployment — Cognigy is one of the more technically credible, well-reviewed platforms in this category. If you're running an SMB ecommerce storefront, look elsewhere.
